scenes.visual: Title card: Calcium Turns Down the Gain.

scenes.tts: Your eyes work in starlight and in sunshine. A photoreceptor manages that by turning its own gain down as the background brightens. Calcium is the signal. Light lowers calcium in the outer segment. Falling calcium speeds the making of c G M P, and lets the active pigment be shut off sooner. That feedback keeps the cell answering to changes in light, instead of saturating.

scenes.visual: A photoreceptor under a background-light bar that brightens; a calcium gauge in the outer segment falls as the bar rises; a gain dial turns down in step; small flash blips on top of the background still produce clear responses instead of a flat saturated trace.

scenes.tts: Light closes channels in the outer segment, so calcium entry falls, while a pump keeps removing calcium. At low calcium, the G CAPs speed c G M P synthesis, which reopens channels. Recoverin lets go of G R K one, the kinase that switches off activated pigment. Both push the cell back toward its dark state while the light stays on. That push is gain control.

scenes.visual: Reuse the existing loop animation: membrane with channel chips that light closes, calcium dots stop entering, a pump chip removes dots, GCAP chip sends cGMP to reopen channels, recoverin chip releases a GRK1 chip acting on an activated-pigment chip; loop arrow labelled gain control. Make the GCAP-to-cGMP arrow the thickest.

scenes.tts: To test a loop, cut it. In mouse rods lacking both G CAPs, responses recover slowly, single-photon responses grow about five times larger, and adaptation to background light is badly impaired. Cones without G CAPs look much the same. So the G CAPs normally curb and shorten each response. In people, G CAP one mutations are linked to severe inherited blinding disease.

scenes.visual: Two rods side by side, control and GCAP knockout with both GCAP chips crossed out; the same single-photon blip gives a small brief trace in control and a trace about five times taller and much longer in the knockout; a small cone pair repeats the pattern; a closing tag reads GCAP1 mutations: inherited blinding disease.

scenes.tts: Sensitivity falls as the background brightens, and two numbers describe the fall. I zero is the background that halves sensitivity, and n sets the slope. Mouse cones lacking the G CAPs and recoverin reach half sensitivity at about a quarter of the control background, and then fall more steeply. Some adaptation remains even so, and what supplies it is still open.

scenes.tts: Rods and cones split the range of light. A rod can respond to a single photon. Cones are less sensitive, but they end each response faster, which suits bright light. Mouse recordings revise one rule. On a bright background, rod-driven responses dip, then recover with continued exposure. So in these mice, rods do not simply switch off in daylight.

scenes.visual: A long horizontal light-level axis from dim to bright; a rod bar covers the dim end and a cone bar the bright end; a rod single-photon blip beside the rod bar and a quick cone trace beside the cone bar; then a mouse tag and a contrast-sensitivity trace that drops when a bright background starts and climbs back over time.

scenes.tts: When photoreceptors die, the order matters. In typical retinitis pigmentosa, rods die first and cones die after, even when the faulty gene is not expressed in cones. Losing cones costs daylight and central vision. One candidate reason is lost rod support. A rod-derived factor, R D C V F, raises cone glucose uptake in experimental models. Oxidative damage is another candidate, and no single cause is settled.

scenes.tts: Gene therapy can now improve vision in some genetic forms. In a randomized trial, R P E sixty-five gene augmentation improved navigation at low light levels over a control group at one year. An early editing study for C E P two ninety reported safety and a possible benefit, without a control group. The design decides what each study can claim.

Right: a single-arm study with one treated eye and the fellow eye untreated, and no control group box. A closing label reads design sets the claim.
